title: Geometric stalk comparison for a coefficient dual
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative noetherian ring, and $F$ a finite locally constant sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant]. For every geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ a separably closed field, there is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules $(\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(F,\Lambda_X))_s\cong\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(F_s,\Lambda)$.

source.place: IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf.ihom_unit docstring, local finite presentation and dual finite generation

proof.text: Lift the geometric point through a member U of a trivializing étale cover. Use isConstant_over_iff_upperStar and the essential-image characterization of constant sheaves to obtain a module M and an isomorphism M_U ≅ F|_U. The pullback-stalk comparison and the constant-sheaf stalk comparison give F_s ≅ M. Transport finite generation of F_s along this isomorphism to obtain Module.Finite Λ M.

Apply the étale dual restriction comparison to F at U. Apply internalHom.mapIso to M_U ≅ F|_U, contravariantly in its first argument. Compose with the constant-module dual comparison for M, obtaining (F^∨)|_U ≅ Hom_Λ(M,Λ)_U.

Apply the stalk functor at the lifted point. Compose the pullback-stalk and constant-sheaf stalk comparisons to obtain (F^∨)_s ≅ Hom_Λ(M,Λ). Precompose linear maps with F_s ≅ M, using LinearEquiv.arrowCongr, to identify the latter with Hom_Λ(F_s,Λ).
